approach.method_basis: The Parent is a graph-based genetic algorithm whose offspring are chosen by Gaussian-process Thompson sampling. Each round of ten it breeds a fresh pool of 160 candidate molecules from a 64-molecule elite. Breeding parents come mostly from the top score quantiles. Offspring are made by joining connected fragments of two parents or by short chains of atom, bond and ring edits. Duplicates are rejected, and so is any offspring that would introduce a sulfur environment its scored parents do not already have. A Gaussian process is trained on every molecule scored so far in the session, using count-based Morgan fingerprints and a Tanimoto-type similarity, and it predicts the whole pool. Ten correlated samples are drawn from its posterior. Each sample picks its best remaining candidate, and those ten molecules are scored. The scores flow back into the training set and the elite.
approach.novelty: This arm deliberately adds no new search behaviour. It is a placebo for a longer 'stalled' period. The run counts consecutive rounds that fail to beat its best score. Once three in a row have failed, it enters a stalled period. As in this round's two companion arms, the period now lasts until two rounds in a row improve instead of ending at the first improvement. Throughout that period the arm draws one extra set of random numbers from the selector's generator and throws it away before the usual draw. From the first stalled round onward, only the selector's luck changes. An earlier placebo did the same, but only until the first improving round. This arm copies that earlier run exactly until the first round where the longer period continues after a single improvement, and then goes its own way. Together the two placebos give two partly shared measurements of how far luck alone moves the five-task, three-seed average at this trigger. The companion arms hold the longer period on top of the two best stall-time rules found so far, a shortlist of the top 40 candidates by predicted score and a four-times larger pool. They, and the seven earlier stall-time rule changes (which moved the average by between -0.014 and +0.011), are then read against these two measurements.

observed_bottleneck: The sulfur-gated Anchor n-1744a1494180 (complete panel mean 0.596453, SD 0.033970) is now being changed only through session-internal stall gates, and every gated delta is read against one law-free path realization. That reference, n-47993ce5d053 (one discarded allocator draw in each batch announced with the K=3 counter at three or more), moved the complete panel by -0.001735 (seed macros -0.012651/-0.000582/+0.008027). The value is a cancellation of cell deltas from -0.033955 to +0.040951 (population SD 0.015407; median_2 task mean 0.220658, -0.002074). Its crude panel scale (about 0.004) is narrower than the law-changing arms' own (about 0.003 to 0.012). The seven law-changing same-trigger deltas (n-61b9b3bfb40d +0.010577, n-e5dba2059cfe +0.007648, n-25b9a57765d8 +0.004664, n-137ec411f54c -0.003338, n-36afb69ebdd1 -0.005132, n-189cd716f027 -0.009718, n-9e5f01d67b9f -0.014192) have population SD 0.008557 and are centred on that single draw. Round 40 lengthens the regime so that it is held until two consecutive improving announced batches. Recomputed from the Anchor's published trajectories, this lifts exposure from 91 to 184 of 435 announced batches (zaleplon_mpo 19/19/24, deco_hop 0/10/0, drd2_docking 5/15/9, median_2 17/6/10, sitagliptin_mpo 18/19/13 for seeds 0/1/2). The entry batch is unchanged, so the held regime first acts exactly where n-47993ce5d053 first discarded: batch 4, 23, 4, 12 on seed 0 (zaleplon, drd2, median_2, sitagliptin); 8, 15, 15, 18, 7 on seed 1 (zaleplon, deco_hop, drd2, median_2, sitagliptin); 6, 19, 8, 17 on seed 2 (zaleplon, drd2, median_2, sitagliptin). deco_hop seeds 0 and 2 never enter. The reference's logged counter agrees with recomputation from its own trajectories in all 15 sessions. On that reference path, a held rule first acts where the reference did not in batch 7, 24, 7, 13 (seed 0), 9, 18, 22, 19, 9 (seed 1) and 12, 22, 9, 19 (seed 2), giving 75 held-only batches. The shared stretch covers 340 of the 2,340 post-trigger evaluations in the 13 exposed sessions, and in none of them had the reference already reached its final Top-1 by the end of the shared stretch. The limiting behaviour is therefore measurement, not a search law. Positions 1 and 2 will produce held-regime deltas on Parents that first leave the Anchor at the same batches. c-median2-task-gain also requires a median_2 gain to stand outside the trigger-matched law-free reference. Yet only one law-free draw exists, at the shorter regime, and nobody knows whether -0.001735 is a typical path-noise value.

adoptions.applicability: The window's held-regime deltas (positions 1 and 2) and the seven K=3 law deltas are single matched differences of a high-variance graph GA plus GP allocator. A second law-free realization at the same first-trigger state is the cheapest repeated measurement the frozen panel allows.
adoptions.borrowed_element: Hold the oracle budget, tasks and seeds fixed across compared runs, and treat a single run difference of a non-deterministic optimizer as uncalibrated until repeated realizations of the unchanged method are measured.

deviations.adopted_setting: One paired realization per protocol Search seed (0/1/2) on each of five tasks, 300 calls and final Top-1. It is identical to the Anchor until each session's first held batch and partly shared with the earlier reference; two dependent law-free panels are read through a bound rule with no significance claim.
deviations.paper_setting: Five independent whole-run seeds per method; mean and SD of AUC Top-10 over 10K oracle calls on 23 tasks.
deviations.reason: Seeds, budget and panel are protocol-owned. The open question is the path noise at the exact divergence point the gated arms share, so the reference must share their prefix rather than redraw whole runs.

adoptions.implementation_change: The Candidate keeps the Anchor's budget, tasks, seeds, batch size and every search law. It differs only by one discarded allocator block per held batch, in FingerprintPosterior.select via the discard_draws argument set by Evolution.suggest from the held-regime state. The result is a second law-free panel read with R1 through the bound interpretation rule.

adoptions.applicability: The unchanged-algorithm contrast is exactly the quantity positions 1 and 2 need, specialized to their divergence point. A second such contrast gives the first, crude look at its spread.
adoptions.borrowed_element: A seed-only comparison of an unchanged algorithm (same configuration, only the random realization differs), used as the reference for how large a difference randomness alone produces between runs.

deviations.adopted_setting: A second paired realization, perturbing only the posterior allocator stream from each session's first held batch, compared cell by cell with the Anchor and with the first realization.
deviations.paper_setting: Ten whole-run trials differing only in the random seed, split into two groups of five and compared by a two-sample t-test.
deviations.reason: This keeps the perturbation at the component and moment the stall-time law changes act on. It keeps the control auditable as law-free and protects the deco_hop sessions that never enter the regime.

deviations.adopted_setting: The breeding generator is not perturbed, and the first held episode is shared with the earlier reference until its first in-regime improvement.
deviations.paper_setting: A new seed perturbs every random source of the run from the start.
deviations.reason: The trigger is frozen to match positions 1 and 2, and one discarded draw per held batch is the registered perturbation. The resulting dependence is stated and quantified (340 of 2,340 post-trigger evaluations) rather than removed.

adoptions.implementation_change: In FingerprintPosterior.select, one torch.randn of the inherited (batch size, pool size) float64 shape is drawn from the selector's own generator after the pool Cholesky and discarded before the inherited allocation draw, in every batch Evolution.suggest marks as held. All laws are unchanged and the passive same-state replay is logged.

adoptions.applicability: The control must cover exactly the batches that positions 1 and 2 govern, so it adopts their exit rule. It adopts nothing from TuRBO's optimization law.
adoptions.borrowed_element: Success-counter hysteresis: a sharpened state entered after consecutive failures persists across batches and is left only after tau_succ consecutive successes, with the counters reset at the change.

deviations.adopted_setting: Announced batches of ten as the unit, entry at K=3 consecutive non-improving batches, tau_succ=2, no trust region, no restart and no law change.
deviations.paper_setting: Per-trust-region success and failure counters that expand or halve the region; the Search Policy review records tau_succ=3 as the default; restarts at a minimum region size.
deviations.reason: The frozen ticket binds tau_succ=2 and K=3 identically for positions 1, 2 and 3. Here the hysteresis only places the discarded draws.

adoptions.implementation_change: Evolution.suggest enters the held regime when the non-improving counter is at three or more. Evolution.observe counts consecutive improving announced batches inside the regime, leaves it after two and resets both counters. The state only decides in which batches select receives discard_draws=1.

literature_review.conclusion: This reuses the frozen round-40 Search Policy review (fixed-budget repeated-run variance control and TuRBO success-counter hysteresis) and the K=3 reference's recorded review (Henderson et al.; Bouthillier et al.). The PMO full text was re-read to confirm its five-run reporting and its remark that graph GA and GP BO vary strongly between runs. The literature supports repeated law-free realizations as the reference for single matched differences, but supplies no magnitude for this benchmark and treats a few realizations as a crude bound. The specific design comes from internal evidence: the second discarded-draw realization at the held regime, its identity with the first reference up to the first held-only batch, and the bound two-point interpretation rule. That evidence is the open question h-2fa4b3d0e8726724, the single realization recorded in h-899be9ec4538ec8c, and the regime recomputation on the published Anchor and reference trajectories.

sources.applicability: This Parent is a graph GA with a GP Thompson-sampling allocator, the two method classes the benchmark singles out for run-to-run variance. That supports treating a single matched panel difference as uncalibrated and measuring a second law-free realization before reading held-regime deltas. It supplies no magnitude, task or setting for this campaign, whose budget, tasks and seeds are protocol-owned.
sources.finding: With a 10K oracle budget across 23 single-objective tasks and 25 methods, most methods reported as state of the art did not beat their predecessors. Results are means and standard deviations of AUC Top-10 over 5 independent runs, and the authors stress that non-deterministic methods need several runs because graph GA and GP BO in particular show relatively large run-to-run variance (full text re-read for this plan).
sources.title: Sample Efficiency Matters: A Benchmark for Practical Molecular Optimization, Gao, Fu, Sun and Coley, NeurIPS 2022

sources.applicability: Here the success-counter exit defines only where this control's discarded draws occur, so the reference matches the exposure of positions 1 and 2. No trust region, shrink, expansion, restart or extra oracle call enters, and no search law changes.
sources.finding: Each trust region keeps counters of consecutive samples that improved or failed to improve the objective. The region is halved after tau_fail consecutive failures and expanded after tau_succ consecutive successes, with the counters reset at each change; the sharpened state therefore persists across batches and is left only after repeated measured success, and a lower bound on the region triggers a restart.
sources.title: Scalable Global Optimization via Local Bayesian Optimization (TuRBO), Eriksson et al., NeurIPS 2019

sources.applicability: This is a direct methodological analogue. An unchanged algorithm that differs only in its random realization is the reference for how large a difference randomness alone produces, and a second realization is the first step toward seeing its spread. Its benchmark, numbers and t-test are not campaign evidence.
sources.finding: In 'Random Seeds and Trials' the authors run 10 trials of one hyperparameter configuration, 'only varying the random seed across all 10 trials', split them into two sets of five, and report that 'the variance between runs is enough to create statistically different distributions just from varying random seeds' (TRPO on HalfCheetah-v1, two-sample t-test t=-9.0916, p=0.0016).
sources.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning that Matters, Henderson, Islam, Bachman, Pineau, Precup and Meger, AAAI 2018 (ar5iv full text of arXiv 1709.06560)

sources.applicability: This supports the stated limit of this arm. It randomizes only one source (the allocator stream after the trigger) and shares part of its path and the whole breeding stream with the first reference, so two such draws understate the spread that randomizing more sources would reveal. No procedure from the paper is implemented.
sources.finding: Modelling the whole benchmarking process, the authors find that variance due to data sampling, parameter initialization and hyperparameter choice markedly impacts results. They also find that an estimator randomizing more sources of variation comes closer to the ideal estimator, at a 51-fold reduction in compute cost.
sources.title: Accounting for Variance in Machine Learning Benchmarks, Bouthillier et al., MLSys 2021 (arXiv 2103.03098)

hypothesis: Neutral path-divergence control at the held stall regime. Track the session's own consecutive non-improving announced-batch counter exactly as the K=3 siblings do: after the ten initial records, a batch is improving when the session best-so-far after it exceeds the value held when it was announced. Enter the held regime when a batch is announced with the counter at three or more. Keep it active for that batch and every following announced batch until two consecutive announced batches have each been improving. Then leave it, resetting both the non-improving counter and the in-regime improving counter to zero. In each announced batch allocated while the held regime is active, draw one standard-normal array of the inherited allocation shape (announced batch size by pool size, float64) from the posterior selector's own seeded generator. Discard it immediately before the inherited correlated Thompson draw, so that batch and every later allocation consume the next unused blocks of the same i.i.d. stream. No law, probability, scale, threshold, pool size, operator, mask, tie rule or admission rule changes. Only the realized allocator path departs: from the Anchor at the same batch as the K=3 reference, and from the K=3 reference at the first held-only batch (held regime active while the counter is below three). Because no law changes, every discard after the first only changes which i.i.d. block a later allocation consumes, not the distribution of the continuation. The arm therefore supplies a second draw of the law-free continuation from the identical first-trigger state, partly shared with the first.

finding_summary.headline: Second luck-only control ran exactly: panel moved +0.0077 against the first control's -0.0017, almost all from one +0.12 sitagliptin cell
finding_summary.insights:
The two luck-only controls are two draws of the same continuation from the same starting state, and they landed 0.0095 apart, at -0.0017 and +0.0077. Their crude two-draw width, 0.0067, is about 78% of the 0.0086 spread among the seven stall-time rule changes tested so far. That is still under the threshold, fixed before the run, at which the spread would be declared indistinguishable from luck, but not by much. Because the two draws share their first stretch and the entire breeding random stream, the width is an underestimate.

Under the interpretation rule fixed before the run, a stall-time change now needs a panel delta above +0.0172 to stand above both controls, or below -0.0112 to stand below both. None of the seven earlier changes clears the upper bar. The top-40 stall shortlist (+0.0106) drops from 'above the single reference' to partial calibration. The longer mutation walks (+0.0076) and the fourfold stall pool (+0.0047) stood above the first control alone, but now sit inside the two-point luck band. They are unidentified, not refuted. Only stall-time crossover removal (-0.0142) stands below both. The held-regime versions of the shortlist and the fourfold pool, run in this same round, should be read against these thresholds.

For the median_2 objective, a gain must now exceed +0.0124 in the three-seed mean to stand above both controls. That is stricter than the campaign's own +0.010 median_2 criterion, because luck alone just moved median_2 seed 0 by +0.029 and the mean by +0.005. The chemistry explains why. On that objective the best molecules all sit on one propylquinoline/bis-lactam framework, within about 0.01 of each other, and late progress consists of single-atom changes to it. So which variant a re-drawn path happens to reach can move a cell by a few hundredths. Sitagliptin is worse: its scoring surface is bimodal, and one re-draw moved one cell by 0.12. Single-cell gains of that size on these objectives cannot be read as mechanism. A real median_2 improvement has to clear that band, and showing it on all three seeds rather than in one cell is the more convincing sign.

Pure luck cost the protected tasks nothing beyond margin. Zaleplon seed 0 fell again (-0.045), so all nine stall-gated Children of this Anchor measured so far, both controls included, give up that cell. That confirms it as a favourable Anchor realization rather than something a change destroys.

Still open: two dependent draws only bracket the width of path noise; they do not measure it. A breeding-stream control or more protocol seeds is the way to an actual estimate. This reference recipe is complete under its review conditions, and a third discarded-draw arm would add another dependent draw rather than new information.
finding_summary.results:
The control behaved exactly as registered, so its score is a valid second reference. Thirteen of fifteen sessions entered the held stall period, the same thirteen as the Anchor and the first control. The deco_hop sessions on seeds 0 and 2 never stalled and reproduced the Anchor record for record, including its 0.856 seed-0 endpoint. Over all 435 announced batches the logged stall state matched a recomputation from the run's own scores. The extra random block was drawn and thrown away in exactly the 184 held batches (21 held periods) and in no other batch. Every held period that ended did so after exactly two improving batches in a row; ten ran to the end of the session. 55 of the 184 held batches raised the session best.

Each session matched the Anchor molecule for molecule up to its first held batch. It matched the first control, whose stall period ended at the first improving batch, up to the first batch the longer period added. At both points the candidate pool and its predicted means and uncertainties were identical. The thrown-away block was bit-for-bit the block the other run had used, and replaying the rule on it reproduced that run's ten picks. The two controls shared 340 of 2,340 post-trigger evaluations, as predicted, and then went separate ways. 93 of the 184 held batches (51%) were batches the first control never touched, and every exposed session had some. Every held batch picked differently from its same-state replay, on average 6.2 of 10 molecules. Only 3.0% of molecules scored after divergence also appear in the Anchor's session, and 6.1% in the first control's. The selection rule itself did not move: the shift in where picks fell on the predicted-score and uncertainty rankings gave test statistics of -1.39 and +1.35, far inside the 3.26 bound. Every pool held 160 candidates and no batch fell back to the backup route.

On the score panel the matched mean went from 0.596453 to 0.604200, a reference delta of +0.007747. Seed macros moved by -0.0055, +0.0260 and +0.0027. Seven cells rose, five fell and three were exactly unchanged. One cell carries almost all of it: sitagliptin seed 1 rose from 0.500 to 0.620 (+0.120), and without it the reference is -0.0003. The other large swings were zaleplon seed 0 -0.045, median_2 seed 0 +0.029, zaleplon seed 2 +0.024, sitagliptin seed 0 -0.015 and median_2 seed 2 -0.011. The SD of the fifteen cell deltas was 0.034, more than twice the first control's 0.015. Measured directly against the first control, this run is +0.0095 higher, with cells from -0.041 to +0.138.

For the Research Brief: the median_2 three-seed mean went from 0.222732 to 0.227889 (+0.0052), with cells +0.029, -0.003 and -0.011. On the protected tasks, deco_hop moved +0.0013, drd2_docking +0.0013, sitagliptin_mpo +0.0351 and zaleplon_mpo -0.0041. None fell below its margin (0.02, 0.03, 0.02, 0.02).

molecular.headline: Inherited fused heteroaromatic cores decorated with N-bound halogen, nitroso, four-membered and macrocyclic rings; no CF3, no stereocentre, no charge.
molecular.overall_character: Read context.molecular_digest and then all fifteen Child trajectories in focus.artifacts.this_node_trajectories (three seeds x five objectives, 300 records each: 10 initial plus 290 optimizer proposals, 870 optimizer proposals per objective, 4350 in total) and all fifteen published Parent trajectories for n-1744a1494180; every listed path exists and was read, and molecular_digest.tasks_without_trajectories is empty, so no objective is omitted. context.comparison reports child_complete true and paired_complete true on matched seeds 0/1/2 against code Parent n-1744a1494180, so the Parent remarks below are complete-pairing chemical observations and never causal, activation or ranking claims. The output is uniformly ring-rich and aromatic: digest ring_closure_rate 0.9609-0.9874 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.9529-0.9724 per objective, mean SMILES length 44.4-57.9, and my own RDKit reading of the same files gives median 26-31 heavy atoms, 381-449 Da and 2-4 aromatic rings. Size and ring count therefore sit inside ordinary medicinal-chemistry range; the decoration does not. Every molecule is parsable (0 of 4350 fail RDKit), but 951 of 4350 carry a halogen bonded directly to nitrogen, 182 a halogen on oxygen, 240 a C- or N-nitroso group, 615 a four-membered ring and 118 are one-to-four-heavy-atom fragments such as ClCl, FF, C or C#C that score at or near the floor. Across all 4350 proposals there is not one trifluoromethyl group, not one piperazine or morpholine ring, not one formal charge and not one defined stereocentre (digest stereocentre_rate and charged_rate are 0.0 on all five objectives), although the sp3-rich set carries about two RDKit-perceived unassigned stereocentres per molecule. The Parent's chemistry is the same family: it emits 24 piperazine-containing molecules where this node emits none, this node places roughly 70 percent more halogen-on-nitrogen in the small-bicyclic objective (464 against 275 of 870) and far fewer S-halogen bonds in the ring-rich objective (18 against 78 of 870), and in two of the fifteen sessions the two nodes propose the identical 300 molecules in the identical order.

per_task.generated_character: 870 optimizer proposals, median 26 heavy atoms and 396 Da, median QED 0.60 and median cLogP 4.0; digest ring_closure_rate 0.9621, aromatic_atom_rate 0.9575, halogen_rate 0.9575, stereocentre_rate 0.0. One family dominates: a 5-6 fused pyrrolo-pyridine or indole core carrying an aryl or heteroaryl carboxamide plus small ethyl, methyl and methoxy decoration, which is the initial-pool indole-2-carboxamide COc1cc2[nH]c(C(=O)Nc3ccc(F)cc3)cc2c(OC)c1OC (0.3051) with its amide N-H replaced by N-F, N-Cl or N-Br. 464 of 870 carry a nitrogen-halogen bond, 577 an amide, 198 a basic amine, only 1 a nitrile and none a CF3. Seed 0 instead reaches a pyrazolo-fused aryl ketone, CCc1c(OC)cc2c3c1NCC3=C(C(=O)c1ccc(Br)cc1)N(Br)N2 at 0.4143, with an N-Br on a ring nitrogen.
liabilities: N-haloamides and N-halo ring nitrogens in 464 of 870 proposals, and in the single best molecule; these are oxidising, hydrolytically unstable groups no chemist would propose as an analogue
12 proposals contain an eight-membered or larger ring and 68 a four-membered ring, both produced by ring edits rather than by design
33 of 870 evaluations are spent on one-to-four-heavy-atom fragments (ClCl, FBr, SBr, C, C#C) that return 0.0
late-session collapse to isosteric halogen permutations: digest evaluations 246, 271, 276 and 285 share one skeleton, differ only in F/Cl/Br identity and all return 0.4718
missing_features: no nitrile anywhere on the dominant core: 1 of 870 proposals contains a C#N, so the cyano-plus-acetamide decoration pattern the gradient's aromatic-amide family would allow is never tested
no N,N-dialkyl amide: the amide nitrogen is substituted only by aryl plus halogen, never by two carbon chains
no trifluoromethyl or difluoromethyl group in 870 proposals, although 95.75 percent of them carry some halogen
no defined stereochemistry at all (digest stereocentre_rate 0.0) and no formal charge (charged_rate 0.0)
no newly closed aromatic five-membered heterocycle: the fused core is inherited from the initial pool and only decorated
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Span 0.0 to 0.4828 with digest median 0.3108. The gradient rewards a compact 24-27 heavy-atom fused bicyclic heteroaromatic with one aryl amide and an alkoxy/alkyl pattern, and it rewards halogen presence without caring where the halogen goes: molecules carrying an N-halogen bond average 0.329 against 0.245 for those without, and 83 percent of the top twenty per seed carry one. Proximity in this scoring surface is deceptive: in the seed-2 final records N=c1c2c(CF)n(C3C(O)=CC=C3CCF)c3c2n(c(=O)n1CF)C3 scores 0.5472 while the two neighbouring final records that put sulfur on that same ring nitrogen instead of a fluoroalkyl group return 0.3486 and 0.0725.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Of 4350 optimizer proposals not one contains a trifluoromethyl group and only 18 contain any difluoromethyl carbon, while 951 carry a halogen bonded directly to nitrogen and 182 a halogen bonded to oxygen. The dependence is strongest exactly where halogen is rewarded: on one objective N-halogenated molecules average 0.329 against 0.245 without, on another 0.266 against 0.162, and 83 and 68 percent of the respective top twenty per seed carry such a bond, including both session-best molecules (CCc1c(OC)nc2c(cc(C(=O)N(F)c3ccccc3)n2F)c1C and COc1ccccc1-n1c(CNF)c2c(=O)n(CCF)c(=N)n(F)c2c1F). The highest-scoring molecule of the whole node carries an O-F hypofluorite (O=c1c2c3n(-c4ncnc5cc(OF)c(Cl)cc45)nc2n(c(=S)n1C(F)OCCl)C3).
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator reaches halogen content by bonding halogen to a heteroatom, and it never builds a polyhalogenated carbon.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Halogen-adding edits should attach halogen to carbon and should be able to install a complete halogenated group (CF3, CHF2, OCF3, polyfluorinated ring) in one move, with N-X, O-X and S-X products refused at admission unless an already-scored accepted parent carried that environment. Any gradient that pays for halogen then becomes reachable through makeable chemistry instead of through oxidising heteroatom-halogen artifacts.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Across 4350 proposals there are zero piperazines, zero morpholines, zero primary sulfonamides and zero CF3 groups; the only sulfonamides present (75 of 870 on one objective) are the inherited initial-pool 3,5-dichlorobenzenesulfonyl prolinamide, and the only nitriles (191 of 870 on another) sit on an inherited core. Where a saturated basic ring would pay, the generator substitutes acyclic trialkylamines and strained aminal cages: on the objective where basic-amine molecules average 0.687 against 0.082 without, all sixty top-twenty-per-seed molecules carry a basic nitrogen yet none carries it in a piperazine (CCCCN(CCc1cc(Br)cc(SC)c1N)C(C)(NC)c1cccc(Cl)c1, CN(C)CCC1(c2cccc(Cl)c2)NCCCCN1CCc1cc(N)cc(Br)c1). The paired code Parent n-1744a1494180 emitted 24 piperazine-containing molecules under the same operators, so the capability is marginal rather than structurally absent.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator has no multi-atom functional-group vocabulary: it cannot insert a named medicinal-chemistry group or saturated heterocycle in one edit.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Add fragment-level insertion and replacement operators drawn from a fixed library of makeable groups and saturated heterocycles, applied as single edits at an attachment point, so one proposal can move a whole group rather than relabel one atom. Single-atom relabeling cannot cross the valley between a decorated inherited core and a different functional class.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Digest stereocentre_rate and charged_rate are 0.0 on all five objectives and no SMILES in 4350 proposals contains an @ or a charged atom, yet RDKit perceives about 1.93 unassigned stereocentres per molecule on the most sp3-rich set (median cLogP 5.4, 29 heavy atoms) and 0.42-0.75 on three others. The search actively creates sp3 and spiro centres - 188 and 318 molecules with an sp3 atom shared by two rings on two objectives - and leaves every one of them unspecified, as in CCNC(CCOc1cc(CF)c2c(F)c1CC2)C1CN(C)C1c1cccc(O)c1.
transferable_gaps.gap: No proposal ever carries defined stereochemistry or a formal charge, so configuration and ionisation are outside the search space.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Operators need stereo-aware atom and bond edits that can set, flip and preserve a configuration through canonicalisation, and an optional charge-state edit so acids, ammonium centres and zwitterions are representable. Until then any objective sensitive to configuration or to ionisation state is unreachable by construction, and the generator cannot even tell two diastereomers apart in its own pool.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 615 of 4350 proposals contain a four-membered ring and 36 a three-membered ring; on one objective 350 of 870 contain an eight-membered or larger ring, and its top ninety molecules contain 46 eight-, 60 nine-, 7 ten- and 6 eleven-membered rings, with the best molecule (CCCc1nc2c(OCC)cc1[nH]c(-c1ccccc1)cc1c2CCN(C)C(=O)CN1C) carrying an eight- and two nine-membered bridges. On another objective 71 four-membered rings appear in the top ninety, including the recurring strained bicyclic in COCCc1c2c(c(C(N=O)Nc3cc4c(N=O)cc3-4)c(C)c1C(C)=O)N=C2. Where a size filter would bite, the data say it is not costly to the score: on one objective four-ring molecules average 0.798 against 0.542 without.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring-forming edits produce strained and oversized rings instead of the five- and six-membered rings the cores need.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring closure and ring expansion need an explicit size and strain admission rule (favour five and six, refuse three and four unless the scored parent had them, cap new ring size) and should prefer closing onto an existing fused system over bridging across it. That makes scaffold-level moves produce candidates a chemist would recognise rather than macrocyclic bridges and fused cyclobutanes.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 118 of 4350 proposals have four or fewer heavy atoms (33, 30, 25, 19 and 11 per objective), such as ClCl, FF, SBr, C#C, C and FCCS. They return the floor of their objective - 0.0 on two objectives, 1e-26 to 1e-21 on another, and a constant 0.5 on the one whose floor is non-zero - and the sub-20-heavy-atom subsets average 0.003, 0.0 and 0.089. They are not confined to early exploration: FCCS appears at evaluation 299 of 300 and CF at 296.
transferable_gaps.gap: A constant fraction of every proposal batch is a one-to-four-heavy-atom fragment with no information content.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Impose a heavy-atom floor and a fragment-validity gate on mutation and crossover output before a candidate enters the proposal pool, and requeue the slot. Each such proposal is an evaluation from a 300-call budget spent on a value the generator could predict without the oracle.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 129 of 870 proposals on one objective contain a genuine cumulated double-bond chain (digest cumulated_double_bond_rate 0.1483), for instance Cn1c(=O)c2c(C3=C=C=CC=C3)n(-c3cc(F)ccc3O)cc2n(C)c1=O, and their mean score 0.238 is above that objective's median of 0.1796. On another, 240 of 870 proposals carry a C- or N-nitroso group and the nitroso subset averages 0.600 against 0.591 without, so the toxicophore is slightly favoured. Aminal centres appear in 238 of 870 on a third objective, including its best molecule (CCCCN(CCc1cc(Br)cc(SC)c1N)C(C)(NC)c1cccc(Cl)c1), and sulfenyl halides in 18 more.
transferable_gaps.gap: Chemically absurd electronic motifs survive because the generator has no internal plausibility filter.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The candidate admission step should run a structural-alert and valence-plausibility screen (cumulated unsaturation, nitroso, aminal, heteroatom-halogen, sulfenyl halide) and treat a flagged product as a failed edit rather than a candidate. Whenever a scoring surface is indifferent to these motifs the search drifts into them, so the restraint has to live in the generator, not in the objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The high-scoring regions collapse to very few frameworks: the union of Murcko scaffolds over the top thirty per seed is 14, 16, 23 and 24 on four objectives (57 on the fifth) against 250-586 scaffolds over all 870 proposals. Seven digest leaders tie to ten decimal places at 0.4828171386373609 on one skeleton and differ only in which halogen sits on the amide or ring nitrogen; elsewhere C(F)OCCl to C(F)F leaves 0.8561477222467935 unchanged and an ester-to-thioester swap leaves 0.6415763673890609 unchanged. Those nine evaluations bought three skeletons.
transferable_gaps.gap: Late search budget is spent re-pricing one molecule through score-identical isosteric swaps.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Give the pool an identity notion coarser than canonical SMILES for interchangeable terminal decorations (halogen-for-halogen, chalcogen-for-chalcogen on the same skeleton), and make a plateau of tied scores trigger scaffold-level rather than substituent-level moves. Evaluations then buy new frameworks instead of re-pricing the one the session already holds.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
